title: Remove Cartesian terminal-artifact retention work from test-run rescan state-lock holds
outcome: Terminal artifact retention no longer performs historical terminal-run by observation scans under the test-run rescan StateInner guard; exact terminal identity/proof semantics are preserved and remaining history-sized rescan work is explicitly recorded.
acceptance: Terminal-artifact retention during a rescan performs no observation-by-terminal Cartesian scan under StateInner. Its additional association work is proportional to changed or unfinished exact artifact associations, and an unchanged pass performs no association matching for unrelated completed history.

Exact run, owner, worktree, run-directory, request identity and terminal-result digest predicates remain enforced. Retention preserves original execution identity, provenance, durable terminal proof, persistence-failure retry, alias ordering and current evidence authority; it creates no verification or durability acknowledgement.

Deterministic witness tests show that adding unrelated completed runs and observations leaves terminal-retention candidate/matcher visits unchanged, while matching unfinished associations settle correctly and wrong-owner, wrong-directory or wrong-request associations are refused. Existing publication, registration, compaction and persistence boundary guards remain green without weaker oracles.

A source inventory explicitly records all remaining history-sized work under the rescan commit guard, including summary projection, compacted-metadata processing, conditional persistence/publication and direct compaction selection. Post-fix runtime evidence distinguishes the cold first scan from subsequent idle backstop scans and reports observed holds honestly; the parent live criterion remains unmet until its own observation passes.
